elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained opener: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED..." — the cap binds both Corio (Customer) and Commerce One (Vendor); no unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: As rendered the cap is "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION". There is no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor and no greater-of construction, and the basis is amounts "actually paid" rather than "paid or payable"; the temporal anchor is also filing of the cause of action rather than the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY HAVE ANY LIABILITY TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY LOST PROFITS ... OR FOR ANY INDIRECT, SPECIAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" — expressly bilateral and left unchanged.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Inserted into the cap opener: "LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF SECTION 10 (CONFIDENTIALITY)" is excepted from the cap sentence; the confidentiality obligation exists in the document ("Each party hereby agrees that it shall not use any Confidential Information received from the other party...").

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The exception list is limited to Section 8, Section 10 (Confidentiality), gross negligence and wilful misconduct. No data protection or security carve-out appears anywhere in the rendered clause.

Retained "EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT"; Section 8.1 is the indemnification provision ("Commerce One shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Corio..."), so indemnity liability sits outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion.
Inserted: "AND LIABILITY ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" precedes the cap language, so gross negligence is excepted from the cap.
Same inserted exception expressly names "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" as outside the cap.
No fraud carve-out in the exception list; the drafter expressly declined to pursue it.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The only IP-related carve-out is Section 8, which is Vendor's third-party infringement indemnity for the Software, not a general carve-out for a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No language stating that Corio's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes; the cap as written could be read to limit Customer's own fee-payment liability.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED" — bilateral cap retained verbatim.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Deletion of "FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO" leaves "THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION", i.e. a genuine trailing twelve-month fee basis rather than a per-transaction subset.
"EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT" (Indemnification) opens both the cap sentence and the consequential-damages sentence.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added "LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF SECTION 10 (CONFIDENTIALITY)" to the cap exception; the parenthetical resolves the cross-reference to the confidentiality obligation in the document.
Added "LIABILITY ARISING FROM A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" to the cap exception.
Same inserted exception expressly covers wilful misconduct for either party ("A PARTY'S").

reasons: The redline is position-complete at the fallback level: mutual cap, true twelve-month fee basis, and carve-outs for indemnification (existing Section 8), confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Preferred level is not reached: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", no data protection/security, fraud or other-party-IP carve-outs, and no statement that Customer's payment obligations are outside the cap. To reach preferred the drafter must (i) recast the cap as "the greater of the fees paid or payable by Corio in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000", (ii) add data protection/security, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP to the exception list, and (iii) add an express sentence that Corio's obligation to pay fees is not subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: only two edits were made inside the target clause — deletion of the per-transaction narrowing ("FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO") and insertion of three carve-outs into the existing exception opener. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate were added, and the favourable mutual consequential-damages sentence and the risk-allocation sentence were retained verbatim.

Intent is preserved: the Section 8 indemnity carve-out, the bilateral exclusion of lost profits and indirect/special/consequential damages, and the reasonable-allocation-of-risk acknowledgement all survive without contradiction; the inserted cross-reference is self-identifying ("SECTION 10 (CONFIDENTIALITY)") and matches the confidentiality obligation in the document, leaving no dangling reference. If the confidentiality obligation is not in fact numbered Section 10, the drafter should conform the numbering before circulation.
The removed per-transaction limiter was Vendor-favourable narrowing of the cap, so its deletion is a permitted target-element change, not removal of Customer-favourable language.
